assessment.nobel_worthiness: Moire flat bands at the magic angle gave a tunable platform for correlated insulators, superconductivity and magnetism in a single carbon material. It is the clearest recent case of theory (continuum-model flat-band prediction) followed by decisive experiment, and it opened a whole field of moire quantum matter. As a theorist I value that the physics is quantitatively modelled and tied to transport and spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery. A three-person split fits, though the experimental first author (not in the supplied credit) and other theory groups complicate fairness.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups for several years. Competing explanations of the superconducting pairing and the nature of the correlated states are still unsettled, but the discovery itself is secure. Timing is reasonable though perhaps early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder persist.
Credit to the experimental first author and other early theorists is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall insulator and the Z2 topological classification gave a new state of matter with protected edge states, later confirmed in three-dimensional topological insulators and ARPES spectra. It is a deep conceptual advance with a quantitative link between band-structure theory and measured spectra, which is my home territory.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theory (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall prediction); Molenkamp's group measured the HgTe edge transport. This is a natural, compact configuration. Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele and Hasan's ARPES work on 3D materials are outside the supplied names, so the allocation has some unresolved edge.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation across materials and probes, with a stable interpretation. The 2016 prize recognised topological phases, so the committee must judge whether this adds enough; I think it does as the materials-facing discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases of matter.
Missing credit for the 3D topological insulator discoverers and for the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT is the standard non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions and combined with DFT (DFT+DMFT) to describe Mott transitions and real correlated materials. This is the theory counterpart of my own field and has lasting methodological impact, though the Nobel criterion of a discovery or invention is more ambiguous for a method.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, Georges and Kotliar built the DMFT mapping onto an impurity model, and Kotliar developed the DFT+DMFT combination. Metzner is not in the supplied credit, which is a real fairness problem; among the supplied names, these three are the sound choice.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use and cross-checks against experiment, yet quantitative predictive power for real materials varies and cluster extensions are still under development. Mature, but the committee historically hesitates over computational methods.
uncertainties: Metzner's decisive contribution is not in the supplied credit.
Whether a method rather than a physical discovery is Nobel-appropriate.
Predictive accuracy for real materials is uneven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in MgO(001) junctions, predicted from first-principles spin-filtering by symmetry-selected Bloch states and demonstrated at room temperature, underlies hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It is a clean example of electronic-structure theory predicting a device effect that experiment then confirmed and industry adopted; it matches my own expertise and values.
assessment.attribution: Butler (and Mathon-Umerski) provided the ab initio prediction in 2001; Yuasa and Parkin independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 2004. The Parkin-Yuasa-Butler split is defensible, but Mathon and Umerski, and Djayaprawira, are omitted, and Parkin's earlier work also relates to the 2007 GMR prize.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with two decades of confirmation and large commercial deployment. Timing is good. Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize makes the incremental scientific novelty a point for debate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR Nobel Prize.
Credit for Mathon and Umerski and for the Tsukuba and IBM experimental groups is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and are poised to redefine the second and test fundamental physics. The idea is original, the realisation is spectacular and the impact on metrology is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built the first Sr clock; Jun Ye drove the performance to the best accuracy and many-body clock physics. A two-person prize is clean, though Hall and Hansch (2005) overlap in frequency-comb metrology and others (Takamoto, Ludlow) are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs confirm the performance, and the technology is mature. A redefinition of the SI second may make the timing especially fitting.
uncertainties: Redefinition of the second is pending, so recognition could be premature.
Overlap with the 2005 prize for laser-based precision spectroscopy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration-corrected electron optics brought sub-angstrom imaging of atomic structure in materials, now routine in solid-state physics, with direct consequences for understanding defects, interfaces and 2D materials. It is an enabling invention with unquestioned impact, though more instrumentation than discovery.
assessment.attribution: Rose proposed the corrector designs, Haider and Urban built the first working corrector in the TEM, and the Rose-Haider-Urban trio matches the Wolf and Kavli recognition. Credit to Krivanek and the STEM corrector line is outside the supplied names, which is a fairness issue.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, widely adopted, with decades of validation. Recognition would be timely or even overdue by the standards of the 1986 Ruska prize.
uncertainties: Instrument invention versus physical discovery weighing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard models with tunable parameters, allowing direct tests of Mott physics, many-body dynamics and, with quantum-gas microscopes, single-site resolved correlations. It is a rich bridge between condensed-matter theory and controlled experiment.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller proposed the Hubbard mapping in 1998, Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-Mott transition in 2002, and Esslinger realised the fermionic Mott insulator and Fermi-Hubbard systems. Greiner is also a strong claimant, so choosing three of four names is a real compromise.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated, but the claim of quantitatively solving open Hubbard problems such as the d-wave superconductivity regime is still partial. Recognition is reasonable but the simulation payoff is still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the quantum simulator has yet answered an open question beyond existing numerics.
Greiner and Jaksch are omitted or not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observation of quantized conductance in steps of 2e^2/h in point contacts demonstrated ballistic transport and Landauer-type conductance, becoming the foundation for quantum point contacts used in spin qubits and edge-channel experiments. The result is simple, clean and quantitatively understood.
assessment.attribution: The 1988 papers by van Wees et al. and Wharam et al. (Pepper's group) were simultaneous. The supplied credit omits Wharam and also Landauer's theoretical underpinning, so a fair two-name configuration is imperfect, and the committee may regard it as an awkward fit.
assessment.maturity: Overwhelmingly confirmed over nearly four decades and entirely stable, but the long gap raises the question of why it was not recognised earlier, and Nobel precedent with the IQHE overlaps.
uncertainties: Wharam and colleagues from the simultaneous Cambridge work are not in the supplied credit.
Possible sense that the discovery is a consequence of earlier Landauer-Buttiker theory.
